page: Amazon Web Services m5d.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based instance configured with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 extensions along with hardware AES encryption. Memory provisioning consists of 384 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4 GB per vCPU without any discrete GPU acceleration.

The instance includes 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core scaling, recording 81,319.36 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 55,443.45 in PassMark CPU measurements. The memory subsystem delivers notable read throughput, exceeding 214 GB/sec in large uncached memory reads, which aligns with strong in-memory key-value performance of 74.41 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks.

A notable tradeoff is the instance's lower single-thread performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,147.0 and bottom-quartile single-core stress-ng results. Consequently, token generation throughput for language models is limited. The system provides strong resource density and cost efficiency for parallelized workloads that benefit from large physical core counts and integrated high-speed NVMe storage, such as relational and NoSQL databases, distributed caching clusters, ETL pipelines, and concurrent build servers.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor delivering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 3.1 GHz. The platform is configured with 384 GB of DDR4 memory, providing a standard 4 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 25 Gbps of baseline networking. A key feature of the configuration is the bundled 3,600 GB local NVMe SSD storage array, which operates without attached discrete GPUs. Benchmark results emphasize strong multi-core compute and high memory bandwidth, achieving over 81,300 in stress-ng multi-core benchmarks and 74.41 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded throughput and sequential tasks remain modest. Given its high aggregate core count and integrated high-speed local disk, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive caching systems, relational databases requiring fast scratch storage, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise application servers.
